$comment: THE single source of truth for colour and base widths. No colour literal belongs anywhere else in this project. Layer fragments reference these as "$color.path.visitor_path". Edit here and refresh the browser - there is no build step.
$comment_look: Hand-tinted historical estate map. Saturated pigment washes (supplied as sprite patterns from pipeline/rules/sprite.json) carry the colour; everything drawn as a LINE stays crisp dark ink so the map reads sharply at any zoom. The solid colours below are the flat base each wash sits on, and the fallback where a class has no pattern - keep them close to the wash base colours in sprite.json or edges will show.

color.$comment_paper: Warm rag paper. Also the halo colour behind labels.
color.$comment_ink: One ink, used at varying weight and opacity for all linework.

building.$comment: Venetian red roof wash, sienna ink outline. `wall` is the shadowed side of the isometric block - the footprint drawn at its true position, with the roof lifted off it.

path.$comment: Buff carriage drives and walks, drawn with a sepia ink casing so they stay crisp over the washes.

width.$comment: Base line widths in pixels at zoom 17. Path widths come from `base_width` on each feature (set in pipeline/rules/classification.json); these are for everything else.

opacity.$comment: Washes are opaque - this is flat 2D artwork, with no terrain beneath to show through.
